name: Pirfenidone
route_note: Oral capsules or tablets three times daily with food, titrated over two weeks
targets: TGF-β signalling (indirect; molecular target not defined)
originator: Marnac Inc.; developed by Shionogi (Japan) and InterMune

discovery.note: A simple pyridone found to have antifibrotic activity in animal models of lung fibrosis.

tagline: Oral antifibrotic that slows lung-function decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
summary: Pirfenidone is an oral antifibrotic drug that slows the decline in lung function in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). With nintedanib, it was one of the first two drugs approved for IPF in the US, on the same day in 2014.
mechanism: Pirfenidone's precise molecular target is unknown. In models it reduces fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis and down-regulates profibrotic and inflammatory mediators, notably transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) and TNF-α.
It also has antioxidant activity. The net effect in IPF is slower loss of forced vital capacity, not reversal of established fibrosis.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Approved in Japan (Pirespa, Shionogi) for IPF.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: EMA approves Esbriet (InterMune) for mild to moderate IPF.

history.title: ASCEND trial
history.detail: Phase 3 ASCEND trial shows reduced FVC decline in IPF.

history.title: US approval and Roche deal
history.detail: FDA approves Esbriet in October, the same day as nintedanib; Roche completes its acquisition of InterMune.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic pirfenidone becomes available in the US.

pk.bioavailability: Food reduces Cmax; absolute value not well defined

serious: Interaction with strong CYP1A2 inhibitors such as fluvoxamine

facts: FDA approved pirfenidone and nintedanib for IPF on the same day, 15 October 2014.
Smoking induces CYP1A2 and lowers pirfenidone exposure.
